entries.title: What each file in a React/Vite project does
entries.summary: A map of the files you will touch most.
entries.when: Opening a project for the first time.

code: index.html            Single HTML page; has <div id="root"> and loads /src/main.jsx
src/main.jsx|.tsx     ENTRY POINT: mounts <App /> into #root (add Router/providers here)
src/App.jsx|.tsx      Top-level component: layout and (often) the routes
src/App.css           Styles for App (template default; optional)
src/pages/            One component per page/route (Home, About, Contact)
src/assets/           Images/fonts you import from code
public/               Static files served as-is at /name.ext (favicon, robots.txt)
node_modules/         Installed packages (never edit, never commit)
steps.label: Typical layout

entries.expected: You know where to look for routes, text, styles and images.
troubleshooting: components/ and pages/ are conventions, not rules - existing projects may differ. Follow what is already there.

code: 1. Search a short, unique piece of visible text (text can be split across JSX lines).
2. No hit? Right-click the element in the browser > Inspect, look at its class name, search that.
3. Still stuck: start at src/main.jsx -> App.jsx -> routes -> pages/ and follow the imports.

Several matches: the one inside a component that is imported by your route is the right one.

entries.title: Change an image (public folder or src/assets)
entries.summary: Two ways to reference images in Vite.
entries.when: Replacing a logo or hero image.
entries.where: Edit the component; put image files in public/ or src/assets/.

steps.label: Option 1: file in public/logo.png - use an absolute path starting with /
Option 2: file in src/assets/logo.png - import it

entries.expected: The new image shows after save.
troubleshooting: Broken image: file name is case-sensitive on Linux/Netlify (Logo.png != logo.png).
Do not write src="src/assets/logo.png" - that path does not exist in the browser.
Always add a meaningful alt text.

entries.title: Create a reusable component
entries.summary: A component is a function that returns JSX; its name must start with a capital letter.
entries.when: The same UI appears more than once, or a file is getting long.
entries.where: Create src/components/Greeting.jsx, then import it where you use it.
entries.expected: Two headings appear. Editing Greeting.jsx changes both.
troubleshooting: Lowercase name (<greeting />) is treated as an HTML tag - capitalise it.
'Failed to resolve import': check the relative path and spelling (./ vs ../).

entries.title: Import and export components (default vs named)
keywords: does not provide an export named
entries.summary: Each file exports what other files can import.
entries.when: Moving code into new files, or fixing import errors.

code: // elsewhere - any name works for a default import
steps.label: Default export (one per file)

code: // elsewhere - names must match, in braces
steps.label: Named exports (many per file)

entries.expected: Imports resolve and the component renders.
troubleshooting: 'does not provide an export named X': you used braces for a default export (or vice versa).
Extensions (.jsx/.tsx) can be omitted in Vite imports; folder imports need an index file.

entries.title: Pass props to a component
entries.summary: Props are inputs to a component, like function arguments.
entries.when: Reusing one component with different content.
entries.where: Component file + the place that uses it.

code: export default function Card({ title, text = 'No description' }) {
steps.label: Component receives props (text has a default)
children: content placed between the tags

entries.expected: Each Card shows its own title and text.
troubleshooting: For non-string values use braces: <Card count={3} active={true} />.
Props are read-only; change data with state in the parent.

entries.title: Manage state with useState
entries.summary: State is data that, when changed, re-renders the component.
entries.when: Anything that changes while the user interacts: counters, toggles, form text.
entries.expected: Clicking increments the number; typing updates the greeting.
troubleshooting: Never change state directly (likes++); always call the setter.
Hooks go at the top level of a component, not inside if/for.
Updating from the previous value: setLikes(n => n + 1).

entries.title: Add click handlers and form submit
entries.when: Making buttons and forms do something.

steps.label: Pass the function, do not call it

entries.expected: Click runs the function; form logs without reloading.
troubleshooting: onClick={handleClick()} runs it immediately on render - drop the ().
Need arguments? Wrap in an arrow function: onClick={() => remove(id)}.

entries.expected: The file exists; it appears in the browser once routed.

entries.title: Set up navigation with React Router
entries.summary: Maps URLs (/, /about, /contact) to page components and adds links that do not reload the page.
entries.when: Multi-page React app, starting from the Vite template.
entries.where: Run npm install in the project root first; edit src/main.jsx and src/App.jsx.

steps.label: 0. Install (skip if already in package.json)
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

steps.label: 1. AFTER: wrap <App /> in BrowserRouter (add the import at the top)

code: import { Routes, Route, Link, NavLink } from 'react-router-dom'
steps.label: 2. Routes and links in App.jsx

entries.expected: http://localhost:5173/about shows About; clicking links changes the page without a full reload.
troubleshooting: 'useRoutes() may be used only in the context of a <Router>': BrowserRouter is missing in main.jsx.
Use <Link to> not <a href> for internal links, otherwise the page reloads.
404 on refresh after deploy: add an SPA redirect (see Running > Netlify).

entries.title: Understand routes: /, /about, /contact, params, layouts
entries.summary: How URL paths map to components, including dynamic and nested routes.
entries.expected: You can read a route table and predict the page for any URL.
troubleshooting: Route order does not matter in v6/v7 (best match wins), but a typo in path gives the 404 page.
Params are always strings.
